doc.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Hobbies and what it means to have made it
summary: The piano is his best diversion; success means doing what he loves, such as playing a good Cherokee chorus.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Do you have any nonmusical hobbies or anything? I ask that because I don’t and I just wondered if there’s something that gets you out of that.

See there’s nothing that’s more refreshing to me than to practice the piano. So whatever I’ve been doing, the best diversion would be to sit down and play. I do work out, I like to exercise, I think to do what I do and do it well it’s a good idea to be in pretty good shape. And if I get a chance to play some softball or throw a football around, I love sports. But I haven’t played golf in 17 years I think. I can’t imagine spending four hours doing anything — if I had those hours I should be at the piano. I couldn’t live with myself. So yeah I don’t have any regular hobby. I’m lucky in that what I love to do best is what I do.
Wow. Good statement. People ask sometimes like when do you know you’ve made it. But if you’re doing what you love and being fairly successful at it—

That’d be the only gauge. Because otherwise you’re chasing something that doesn’t have any definition. Because even if you’ve made it in other people’s eyes, it may not have been the way that you intended to and so it feels like you missed the mark somehow. So I’m going to try not to ponder when and if I’ll ever make it. I mean if I can play a nice chorus of “Cherokee” I’ve made it for that day.
Yeah, you get one of these from Herb Ellis.
